subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents

steps: Place the decimal point after the first nonzero digit: $5.4$.
Count how many places the point moved from $54\,000.$ to $5.4$: $4$ places to the left.
Moving left gives a positive exponent, so the power of $10$ is $10^{4}$.
Therefore $54\,000 = 5.4 \times 10^{4}$.
A positive exponent $10^{5}$ means move the decimal point $5$ places to the right.
Starting from $3.6$, move the point right $5$ places, filling in zeros: $360000$.

items.prompt: Compute $(2 \times 10^{3})(4 \times 10^{5})$. Give your answer in scientific notation.

steps: Multiply the coefficients: $2 \times 4 = 8$.
Combine: $8 \times 10^{8}$.
The coefficient $8$ is in $[1,10)$, so no re-normalization is needed.

items.prompt: Compute $\dfrac{9 \times 10^{7}}{3 \times 10^{2}}$. Give your answer in scientific notation.

steps: Divide the coefficients: $9 \div 3 = 3$.
Subtract the exponents: $10^{7} \div 10^{2} = 10^{7-2} = 10^{5}$.
Combine: $3 \times 10^{5}$.
The coefficient $3$ is in $[1,10)$, so the answer is already normalized.

items.prompt: Compute $(5.1 \times 10^{6}) + (2.4 \times 10^{6})$. Give your answer in scientific notation.

steps: Both terms share the same power of $10$, namely $10^{6}$.
Add the coefficients: $5.1 + 2.4 = 7.5$.
Keep the common power of $10$: $7.5 \times 10^{6}$.
The coefficient $7.5$ is in $[1,10)$, so the answer is normalized.

items.prompt: Compute $(6 \times 10^{4})(5 \times 10^{3})$. Give your answer in scientific notation.

steps: Multiply the coefficients: $6 \times 5 = 30$.
Add the exponents: $10^{4} \times 10^{3} = 10^{7}$, giving $30 \times 10^{7}$.
The coefficient $30$ is not in $[1,10)$, so re-normalize: $30 = 3 \times 10^{1}$.

items.prompt: Compute $\dfrac{2 \times 10^{5}}{8 \times 10^{2}}$. Give your answer in scientific notation.

steps: Divide the coefficients: $2 \div 8 = 0.25$.
Subtract the exponents: $10^{5} \div 10^{2} = 10^{3}$, giving $0.25 \times 10^{3}$.
The coefficient $0.25$ is less than $1$, so re-normalize: $0.25 = 2.5 \times 10^{-1}$.

items.prompt: Compute $(4 \times 10^{-3})(2 \times 10^{-5})$. Give your answer in scientific notation.

steps: Multiply the coefficients: $4 \times 2 = 8$.
Add the exponents, keeping the signs: $-3 + (-5) = -8$, so $10^{-3} \times 10^{-5} = 10^{-8}$.
Combine: $8 \times 10^{-8}$.
The coefficient $8$ is in $[1,10)$, so the answer is normalized.

items.prompt: Compute $(8 \times 10^{5}) + (3 \times 10^{4})$. Give your answer in scientific notation.

steps: The powers of $10$ differ ($10^{5}$ and $10^{4}$), so rewrite one term to match.
Rewrite $3 \times 10^{4}$ with exponent $5$: $3 \times 10^{4} = 0.3 \times 10^{5}$.
Add the coefficients over the common power: $8 + 0.3 = 8.3$, giving $8.3 \times 10^{5}$.
The coefficient $8.3$ is in $[1,10)$, so the answer is normalized.
Place the decimal point after the first nonzero digit: $4.7$.
Count how many places the point moved from $0.000\,047$ to $4.7$: $5$ places to the right.
Moving right gives a negative exponent, so the power of $10$ is $10^{-5}$.

items.prompt: A red blood cell has a diameter of about $8 \times 10^{-6}$ m. If $0.0005$ of these cells are lined up end to end, how long is the line? Give your answer in scientific notation, in meters.

steps: First write the decimal quantity in scientific notation: $0.0005 = 5 \times 10^{-4}$.
Multiply the two quantities: $(5 \times 10^{-4})(8 \times 10^{-6})$.
Multiply the coefficients: $5 \times 8 = 40$. Add the exponents: $-4 + (-6) = -10$, giving $40 \times 10^{-10}$.
Re-normalize: $40 = 4 \times 10^{1}$, so $40 \times 10^{-10} = 4 \times 10^{-9}$.
The line is $4 \times 10^{-9}$ m long.

items.prompt: The Sun's mass is about $2 \times 10^{30}$ kg and Earth's mass is about $6 \times 10^{24}$ kg. About how many times more massive is the Sun than Earth? Give your answer in scientific notation, rounded to two significant figures.

steps: To find how many times larger, divide the Sun's mass by Earth's mass: $\dfrac{2 \times 10^{30}}{6 \times 10^{24}}$.
Divide the coefficients: $2 \div 6 = 0.333\ldots$. Subtract the exponents: $30 - 24 = 6$, giving $0.333\ldots \times 10^{6}$.
Re-normalize: $0.333\ldots = 3.33\ldots \times 10^{-1}$, so $0.333\ldots \times 10^{6} = 3.33\ldots \times 10^{5}$.
Round to two significant figures: $3.3 \times 10^{5}$.
The Sun is about $3.3 \times 10^{5}$ times more massive than Earth.

items.prompt: Light travels about $3 \times 10^{8}$ meters per second. How far does light travel in $2 \times 10^{3}$ seconds? Give your answer in scientific notation, in meters.

steps: Distance equals speed times time: $(3 \times 10^{8})(2 \times 10^{3})$.
Multiply the coefficients: $3 \times 2 = 6$. Add the exponents: $8 + 3 = 11$, giving $6 \times 10^{11}$.
The coefficient $6$ is in $[1,10)$, so no re-normalization is needed.
Light travels $6 \times 10^{11}$ m.

items.prompt: A computer chip transistor is about $7 \times 10^{-9}$ m wide. Express this width in nanometers, where $1$ nanometer $= 10^{-9}$ m.

steps: We want the width in nanometers, so divide by the size of one nanometer: $\dfrac{7 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}}{10^{-9} \text{ m/nm}}$.
Divide the coefficients: $7 \div 1 = 7$. Subtract the exponents: $-9 - (-9) = 0$, giving $7 \times 10^{0}$.
Since $10^{0} = 1$, the result is $7 \times 1 = 7$.
The transistor is $7$ nanometers wide, a more natural unit than meters.

items.prompt: A data center stores $4.5 \times 10^{14}$ bytes of data. Each hard drive holds $9 \times 10^{11}$ bytes. How many hard drives are needed to store all the data? Give your answer in standard form.

steps: Divide the total data by the capacity of one drive: $\dfrac{4.5 \times 10^{14}}{9 \times 10^{11}}$.
Divide the coefficients: $4.5 \div 9 = 0.5$. Subtract the exponents: $14 - 11 = 3$, giving $0.5 \times 10^{3}$.
Re-normalize: $0.5 = 5 \times 10^{-1}$, so $0.5 \times 10^{3} = 5 \times 10^{2}$.
Convert to standard form: $5 \times 10^{2} = 500$.
The data center needs $500$ hard drives.
